observations.observation: After the operator moved the host hunter to the End near 0.5,100,0.5, the parent directly saw a dragon-magic death notice. The host returned to the overworld, later re-entered the End, and recovered a dropped tracker.
observations.limits: The later re-entry may have involved user input. Inventory count returning to one does not establish automatic tracker re-grant; the operator observed recovery of a dropped item. The raw probe records state and drop events, not the complete causal input sequence.

observations.observation: The operator applied resistance to all connected players, gave the runner a diamond sword, applied strength to the runner, and moved the runner to the End before requesting a direct sword hit on the dragon head.
observations.reportedUnsubmittedInput: An initial bow command was being entered when the command UI closed; the parent reports it was not submitted.
observations.resultAtPreparation: At preparation time the requested direct sword hit was not a completed dragon kill or runner victory.

observations.observation: The user reported difficulty with direct combat and explicitly asked the operator to perform the kill. The operator then submitted /kill @e[type=minecraft:ender_dragon] in the End and directly observed the runner victory notice with match time 21:44 while the runner remained alive.
observations.resultScope: Actual command-triggered dragon death event followed by runner victory; direct sword-combat dragon kill remains unverified.

limits: The trial uses a QA world copy, supplied equipment, amplified effects, and command-based dimension placement. It is not a complete survival progression or ordinary difficulty combat E2E test.
The probe does not record dragon health, dragon attacker identity, command inputs, effect receipt, or weapon hits. The result keeps UI/user evidence and periodic numeric observations separate.
The image is referenced by basename only and is not approved for public publication.
